record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For explicit target sets in the maximal distance minimizer problem, determine all MDMs. Test cases include discs or balls B_R in R^d for d>=2, rectangle boundaries for small r>0, and regular n-gons, where the expected polyline structure is not fully proved even for n=3.

evidence.quote: Question 1.3. What is the set of MDMs for any explicit set you like?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a non-empty compact set and let $r > 0$. For a closed set $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, define
$$F_M(\Sigma) = \sup_{y \in M} \mathrm{dist}(y, \Sigma), \qquad \mathrm{dist}(y,\Sigma) = \inf_{x \in \Sigma} |y-x|.$$
A maximal distance minimizer (MDM) for the pair $(M, r)$ is a connected compact set $\Sigma^* \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected compact sets $\Sigma$ satisfying the covering constraint $F_M(\Sigma) \le r$, i.e.
$$\Sigma^* \in \arg\min\{\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma) : \Sigma \text{ connected, compact, } F_M(\Sigma) \le r\}.$$

Determine, explicitly, the set of all MDMs in each of the following cases:
(a) $M = B_R \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is a closed ball of radius $R$, for $d \ge 2$ and all $r \in (0,R)$;
(b) $M$ is the boundary of a rectangle in $\mathbb{R}^2$, in the regime of small $r > 0$;
(c) $M$ is a regular $n$-gon in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., its boundary or its closed convex hull), for each $n \ge 3$ and all $r > 0$ (it is conjectured that each MDM is a finite polyline whose junctions form angles at least $2\pi/3$; prove or disprove this and identify the minimizers explicitly, including the case $n = 3$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of explicitly determining all maximal distance minimizers for discs/balls, rectangle boundaries (for small r), and regular n-gons remains open. General regularity results are known (MDMs are finite unions of simple curves meeting at angles at least 2π/3), and partial work exists for rectangles, but explicit complete classification—even for the equilateral triangle (n=3)—has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: For n ≥ 6, the MDM for a regular n-gon is expected to be just a poly-line… no clean proof has been written yet.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit MDMs for regular n-gons are conjectured but unproven.

status_evidence.title: Maximal distance minimizers for a rectangle
status_evidence.snippet: Study of MDMs for rectangle target sets.
status_evidence.claim: Rectangle case is partially studied but not fully resolved for all small r.

status_evidence.title: On regularity of maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity results: finite union of simple curves with angles ≥ 2π/3.
status_evidence.claim: Only general regularity is known; explicit classification for discs/balls is not.
